title: Swarm Alignment Hackathon

questions.text: What does a multi-agent sandbox need so that agents cannot leave it, and how would you test that it holds?

Can you build a small, reproducible environment where 5–20 LLM agents acting for different principals share a resource, a market or a tool over many rounds, and log everything so another team can rerun it?
How far can a small, cheap model stand in for a frontier agent in the same environment? At which point do the results stop matching?
What would make a result from your sandbox transfer to real deployments, and what test would show you that it does not?
Under what conditions do leaders, roles and division of labour emerge in an agent population, and can you reproduce it in a safe sandbox?
Do agents that each refuse a harmful task complete it once the task is split across them?
If one agent in a network is compromised, how fast and how far does the bad behaviour spread? Does the shape of the network matter?
As you add agents, mix different models or change who can talk to whom, do cooperation and failure rates change smoothly, or is there a sudden jump?
How should an agent ID work when agents can rename, copy or fine-tune themselves, and how would you revoke one?
What can one malicious agent do inside an existing agent-to-agent protocol such as A2A? Can you demonstrate an attack and propose a fix?
Can you build a reputation score for agents that a group of colluding agents cannot easily game? Show it by attacking it.
Can two agents make a credible commitment without a trusted third party, for example by handing the deal to a sub-agent whose code the other side can check?
Using the Swarm Traces payloads or the AI Village transcripts, can you build a tool that finds coordination, information spread or covert channels in real multi-agent logs?
Can you design oversight that still works when agents can edit or delete the logs it relies on?
Can a monitor that sees only part of the messages between agents detect collusion or hidden (steganographic) communication?
Do AI control protocols, such as a trusted model monitoring an untrusted one, still hold when the untrusted side is several agents that can coordinate?

ai_policy: Use AI tools however they help you: to check your reasoning, find gaps in a draft, write and debug code, or help with the writing. Your team is responsible for everything in the report, and made-up results or references can disqualify a project. Judges score each report on the rubric, and a judge can decline to score one too unclear to follow.
